milestone.title: Post-rc polish — TUI overflow hit-test (B-39), sidebar_focused rename (B-40), follow_ups residue (B-41), confidence validation (B-45)

intent.outcome: After this milestone, the non-blocking cleanup from the M91/M81/M96 and M100-M103 review passes is closed out: the raul TUI tab bar handles overflow correctly across the full narrow-window range (successor to M91's R-9, which R-3 partially fixed for compact-mode), the field/method names match their post-M91 meaning (full sidebar → tab_bar rename across 5 names × ~40 occurrences), the on-disk milestone files carry no dropped-schema residue (follow_ups + 8 other dropped keys stripped), and the findings model validates confidence at the same layer severity is validated.

problem.description: Four review findings are real but non-blocking for the rc release. They span TUI rendering (B-39: overflow hit-test divergence — successor to M91 external review's R-9 finding, R-3 only fixed the < 60 cols compact-mode case), naming hygiene (B-40: App::sidebar_focused and its 4 sibling names — toggle_sidebar_focus, sidebar_move_up/down, handle_sidebar_key — no longer mean sidebar after M91's tab-bar shell), data residue (B-41: 85/108 milestone files still carry empty follow_ups:[] arrays despite M82 dropping the key), and model validation (B-45/F-4: Finding.confidence accepts any string). Each is low-to-medium severity and none block the rc, but leaving them open turns review findings into permanent debt.

in_scope: B-39 (medium, R-9 successor from M91 review): extract the visible-window layout from render_tab_bar into a shared helper so tab_hit_test knows which tabs were drawn and at which columns; the narrow-overflow subset + ◂/▸ indicators + … ellipsis case must be covered (R-3 only fixed the compact-mode < 60 cols heuristic). Add a regression test for click-on-hidden-tab.

B-40 (low): full rename of 5 names × ~40 occurrences: App::sidebar_focused → tab_bar_focused; App::toggle_sidebar_focus → toggle_tab_bar_focus; App::sidebar_move_up → tab_move_up; App::sidebar_move_down → tab_move_down; handle_sidebar_key → handle_tab_bar_key. Sources: crates/raul/src/tui/{render.rs, runner.rs, app.rs} and tests/{tui_sidebar.rs, tui_tab_bar.rs, tui_mouse.rs, board_view.rs, tui_responsive.rs, welcome_overview.rs, truncation.rs}. Land as a single rename commit (the prior decision to defer was for blast radius; M91's own R-3/R-4/R-5 remediation did not retake this work).

B-41 (low): add `mp edit strip-dropped-keys` one-shot utility. Strips DROPPED_CEREMONY_KEYS (currently {behavior, context, requirements, success_criteria, assumptions, interface, risks, technical_context, follow_ups}) from all milestone files in scope. Idempotent — re-running is a no-op. Asserts post-run: grep -c '"follow_ups": \[\]' master-plan/milestones/*.json returns 0 AND mp validate --summary stays 0/0.

B-45 (low, model-layer only): add is_valid_confidence() helper at the model layer and validate confidence in add_finding_with_phase (crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:433) mirroring the existing severity guard at reviews.rs:454-456. Define valid set as {low, medium, high} plus empty-string (the current default when no confidence is set). Does not depend on M101 — confidence's CLI shape is M101's scope; B-45 is the model + add_finding layer guard only.
out_of_scope: Any new TUI feature work beyond the B-39 hit-test fix
Bulk lifecycle migration application to the 108 milestones (separate from B-41 follow_ups sweep; depends on M104 landing first)
The CLI surface for confidence (M101 lands that). B-45 is the model + add_finding layer guard.

design_decisions.rationale: B-41 (follow_ups residue sweep) touches the same milestone files that the bulk lifecycle migration (M104) will rewrite; doing the sweep after M104 lands avoids a double-write. M107 is the external-review remediation chain (verifier-cancellation defense in depth). M91 is the source of B-40's rename debt — its design decision (`sidebar_focused` to limit blast radius across ~25 references) explicitly defers the rename to a follow-up, and M91's R-9 explicitly defers B-39 to a dedicated TUI milestone. Coordinating M91 + M105 avoids re-litigating layout decisions M91 is settling. The other items (B-41, B-45) have no real dependency but M91 keeps the post-rc polish in one shippable set.

design_decisions.choice: Treat B-39 as the canonical follow-up to M91 review's R-9 finding. Coordinate with M91's tab_bar shell.
design_decisions.rationale: M91 landed the tab-bar shell (S1–S7) and the R-3 / R-4 / R-5 remediations; M91 review explicitly filed R-9 (overflow render diverges from tab_hit_test at narrow widths) as deferred to a dedicated TUI milestone. M105 is that milestone. We don't re-litigate M91's compact-mode < 60 cols heuristic that R-3 already wired; B-39 covers the wider overflow-subset + indicators case that R-3 does not.

design_decisions.choice: tab_bar_focused (and 4 sibling renames: toggle_tab_bar_focus, tab_move_up, tab_move_down, handle_tab_bar_key)
design_decisions.rationale: focused_pane was considered but is too generic now that the board pane exists. tab_bar_focused is unambiguous and matches the render function name (render_tab_bar). Sibling renames are derived mechanically (sidebar → tab_bar in move methods, handle_sidebar_key → handle_tab_bar_key to match the new field name). The renames are complete — no 'sidebar' alias is preserved.

design_decisions.choice: Single rename commit covering all 5 names × ~40 occurrences. Same shape as M97's lean-milestones rename pattern.
design_decisions.rationale: Splitting into per-file or per-method commits would create intermediate states where the field name and the methods/move calls would diverge (a half-renamed state would fail tests). Single commit is atomic and reviewable; the test surface is rewritten alongside the production rename.

design_decisions.choice: `mp edit strip-dropped-keys` one-shot utility in the mp runtime
design_decisions.rationale: The bug is one-shot (the validate_create_milestone_keys guard already prevents new writes carrying dropped keys; only the 85 historical files need cleaning). The utility strips every key in DROPPED_CEREMONY_KEYS from every milestone file in scope. Idempotent by construction: re-running the utility on a clean plan is a no-op (no key matches, no file rewrites). Adding it to `mp edit` rather than a new top-level subcommand keeps the namespace surface area flat — `mp edit` is the right place for milestone-shape mutations.

design_decisions.choice: Model-layer + add_finding layer only. Does not depend on M101.
design_decisions.rationale: Finding::confidence is currently `String` with a 'low | medium | high' comment but no validation. The guard belongs at the same architectural layer as the severity guard in reviews.rs:454-456 — i.e., inside add_finding_with_phase plus an is_valid_confidence() helper. The CLI surface for confidence (M101 AC-08) is a different concern; B-45 establishes the model invariant that M101 will respect via tests.
